account: Today I have office business at eight, a grain inspection at the mill at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at one, tea at the neighbour's east-bank cottage at three, and Builder's findings at sixteen thirty. Builder is conducting an authorized preventive inspection of town hall doors, bridge decking, and the east ferry landing for two emeralds total. No confirmed defects have been reported, and no repairs or extra charges are authorized. There has been repeated confusion over which landing and how to write the findings: Builder has no book or funds, and the secretary says no writable office book is available. I have clarified the east landing and asked the secretary to transcribe the findings for Builder's review without extra expense. This appears to be an administrative difficulty, not evidence of a safety emergency. The secretary has now relayed the landing clarification to Builder. Baker is waiting nearby holding emeralds; I do not yet know his business. Neighbour says Freight was asking when to expect my mill visit and will be at the east landing this morning. I do not yet know why Freight needs that information. Neighbour also confirmed our usual three-o'clock tea.
